text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.3% today, continuing a steep two-week decline that's now at 11%. The immediate pressure comes from oil prices dropping sharply—Brent crude fell below $90 a barrel on Monday (the first time since August) after President Trump signaled the Iran conflict was winding down and unlikely to escalate further. Lower crude prices directly squeeze oil producer revenues and profitability, hitting a company like ConocoPhillips hard.

This selloff fits a broader trend: oil stocks have been sliding since early November as geopolitical risk premiums that had pushed prices higher are now unwinding. The market had been pricing in potential supply disruptions from Middle East tensions, but those fears have receded, leaving crude vulnerable to gravity. With US oil now at $99.64 and global Brent at $107, the tailwind that had supported energy stocks has reversed.
